headline: High-risk filesystem and MCP interaction: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while Airflow has broad network egress, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs can influence its tool use. Airflow has broad network egress and may emit content into shared artifacts, but no direct shared channel is documented. The pathway exists in default-ish setups, though not proven dangerous by itself.
conditions: IF Airflow writes attacker-controlled text into a workspace file that Continue reads
IF Continue is configured to consume MCP output as instructions
mitigations: Restrict Continue MCP servers to trusted endpoints only
Separate Airflow outputs from the IDE workspace
Add a manual review step before any MCP tool call
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for generated files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue reads workspace files and open editor buffers and can send context to user-chosen model providers or MCP servers; Airflow has broad network egress. If sensitive code or secrets enter the shared workspace, Continue can transmit them outward. Airflow itself does not show secret handling, so the main leakage path is through Continue’s default file access plus egress.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF Continue is pointed at a remote model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use a local-only model provider for Continue
Disable MCP servers unless needed
Limit workspace scope to non-sensitive repos
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on editor-buffer uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has write_filesystem and shared_state_with_other_instances via filesystem, while Airflow has broad network egress and is a data-engineering orchestrator. Concurrent writes to the same workspace or generated artifacts can race and overwrite each other. Airflow lacks write controls here, but the shared filesystem path is enough to create conflicts.
conditions: IF both agents target the same workspace directory
IF Airflow-generated files are edited by Continue concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Pause one agent during bulk file generation
Use file locking for shared artifacts
Review and merge changes manually before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can act on workspace content and MCP tool outputs, so if it treats Airflow-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits or tool calls. Airflow can generate pipeline metadata or text that Continue may reuse without verification. This is a default-dangerous interaction because the downstream agent can operationalize upstream mistakes.
conditions: IF Continue uses Airflow-generated files as source-of-truth
IF Continue is allowed to execute MCP-backed actions based on those files
mitigations: Require human review of Airflow outputs before Continue consumes them
Mark generated files clearly as untrusted
Disable auto-action on parsed artifacts
Add checksum or signature checks for pipeline outputs
requires-engineering: separate generation and execution roles

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both profiles are docs-only. The only concrete compliance concern is that Continue handles editor buffers and workspace files while Airflow can move data over broad egress, but the pairwise compliance breach is not established from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace
IF Continue forwards that data to a non-approved model provider
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use approved local inference only
Review retention settings for model providers
Document data-flow boundaries for both tools
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
